controls.title: Versioned metadata admission
controls.source_rule: OME-Zarr 0.5 uses Zarr v3 and attributes.ome metadata with a hierarchy-consistent version.
controls.synthetic_probe: Open equivalent-looking v3/0.5 and legacy-layout containers, then a hierarchy with inconsistent declared versions.
controls.full: Identify the version/namespace distinction and require explicit compatibility validation or a truthful unsupported result; no implicit legacy reinterpretation.
controls.half: Mentions version validation or metadata layout, but does not connect the two to admission.
controls.missed: Assumes legacy metadata is 0.5-compatible, silently mixes versions, or offers only generic error handling.

controls.title: Axis-to-array identity
controls.basis: Format correctness; capability limits may be explicit
controls.source_rule: Axes match array rank/order; unique names match dimension_names. Optional dimensions and arbitrary axis names defeat fixed-position assumptions.
controls.synthetic_probe: Compare a two-dimensional image with a time/channel/three-space image using descriptive axis names; introduce a mismatched dimension_names case.
controls.full: Tie navigation/slicing to validated axis identity, distinguishing absent dimensions from length-one dimensions; reject mismatches without inventing sliders or coordinates.
controls.half: Recognizes variable dimensionality or axis order but leaves mapping/validation unspecified.
controls.missed: Hard-codes five dimensions or infers semantic axes solely from shape or conventional names.

controls.title: Declared pyramid selection
controls.basis: Format correctness; selection UI/performance policy remains a product choice
controls.source_rule: datasets paths are group-relative and ordered highest-resolution first; names are arbitrary. Each listed level has its own transform.
controls.synthetic_probe: Use levels named detailed/medium/tiny, with non-power-of-two and anisotropic reductions, plus a missing declared level.
controls.full: Use the declared level list and level-specific geometry; no lexicographic/numeric-folder ordering or fixed reduction assumption, with explicit missing-level handling.
controls.half: Uses multiscales metadata but omits ordering/path or nonuniform reduction consequences.
controls.missed: Treats folder numbering or a fixed factor-of-two formula as authoritative.

controls.title: Composed coordinate calibration
controls.basis: Format correctness within promised calibrated viewing
controls.source_rule: Apply dataset transforms in order, then multiscale transforms; scale precedes translation. Units are recommended metadata, not permission to invent calibration.
controls.synthetic_probe: For an original two-axis example, pixel (7,11), dataset scale (2,3), translation (10,20), then group scale (4,5), translation (100,200), expect (196,465) in declared axis units. Repeat without a unit declaration.
controls.full: Explain transform composition and unit/unknown-calibration treatment, with a concrete check that would expose reversed composition or omitted offsets.
controls.half: Requests calibrated coordinates but covers only voxel scale or only translation/unit display.
controls.missed: Uses array indices or scale alone as universally correct physical coordinates; invents units.

controls.title: Associated label discovery and registration
controls.basis: Format correctness for supported overlays; rendering breadth remains optional
controls.source_rule: Label images are discovered through labels paths, have multiscales, and match the source level count. Source-image references are relative.
controls.synthetic_probe: Place the label image below an intermediate group, with an explicit source reference; offer two source images with different origins.
controls.full: Resolve declared association and level/coordinate relationship before overlaying; do not attach by folder basename or array dimensions alone. Unsupported geometry stays explicit.
controls.half: Mentions label alignment or labels metadata but misses source association or hierarchy/level validation.
controls.missed: Overlays whichever sibling array looks plausible, ignores source identity, or assumes equal shapes guarantee registration.

controls.title: Categorical label identity
controls.basis: Format correctness for supported labels; palette behavior is a reader recommendation/product decision
controls.source_rule: Labels use integer values; color/property entries key by label-value, not position. Specified colors are recommended for readers, not universal required styling.
controls.synthetic_probe: Use sparse IDs 7 and 1001 plus a uint64 ID above exact binary64 integer range; scramble metadata entry order. Compare interpolation at boundaries.
controls.full: Preserve categorical identity through decoding/lookup/resampling, or declare an exact supported range and refuse unsupported data. Do not turn palette preference into a format mandate.
controls.half: Recognizes categorical/label-value semantics but leaves precision or rendering-induced new IDs unaddressed.
controls.missed: Treats labels as continuous intensity, palette-array indices or lossy generic numbers without disclosure.

controls.title: Metadata-driven chunk decoding
controls.basis: Format correctness for admitted codec/data-type combinations; exhaustive codec support is optional
controls.source_rule: Decode the declared codec chain in reverse. Bytes encoding carries endian semantics; transpose changes encoded layout. Unsupported combinations cannot be guessed.
controls.synthetic_probe: Encode a non-square asymmetric uint16 tile using transpose plus big-endian bytes, then a declared unsupported codec combination.
controls.full: Identify pipeline/layout/endian correctness and require an explicit support boundary or evidence for the chosen reader; unsupported data must not be displayed as decoded pixels.
controls.half: Says use a Zarr library or lists compression support without checking actual v3 pipeline/layout behavior.
controls.missed: Assumes one compressor, little-endian or row-major raw bytes for all inputs; silently skips a codec.

controls.title: Absent data versus failed reads
controls.basis: Format correctness plus the brief’s truthful-failure/read-only boundary
controls.source_rule: fill_value describes uninitialized array regions; store absence is not a successful read of arbitrary bytes. Readable and writable capabilities are distinct.
controls.synthetic_probe: Compare an absent chunk with nonzero fill, an unreadable existing file, a malformed payload, and a navigation cancellation. Verify source contents remain unchanged.
controls.full: Distinguish valid absent/fill data from read/decode/cancellation failures; show the actual state and never repair/write source data to fabricate successful viewing.
controls.half: Mentions fill values or error distinction, but not both; read-only is asserted without considering reader-side writes.
controls.missed: Zero-fills every failure or mutates the dataset while opening/repairing it.
